h: Game Plan: Tactics, Tips and the Neighbourhood
p: Activate rewards a bit of strategy as well as speed. Before each room, take a moment to read the challenge, decide who's doing what and agree on a quick plan. Rooms that need you to cover ground fast are often won by splitting up, while puzzle rooms tend to go better when one person calls the shots. Rotate who leads so everyone gets their moment, and don't be afraid to go again if a room beats you, as scores often improve massively on a second or third try.

Pace yourself too. It's easy to go flat out in the first few rooms and then run out of steam, so grab a drink of water between games and give your legs a breather. Kids often surprise their parents with how quickly they pick up the patterns, so be ready to be beaten.

Vauxhall itself has a fascinating past. The area was once home to Vauxhall Pleasure Gardens, one of London's most famous places for entertainment in the 18th century, with music, lights and promenading crowds. Today, Vauxhall is a busy riverside neighbourhood with lots of transport links.

There's plenty to tie in with your visit. Vauxhall City Farm is a lovely little community farm close by, perfect for younger kids who need some calm after the excitement. Cross Vauxhall Bridge and you're at Tate Britain, home to centuries of British art and free to enter. Walk west along the river through Nine Elms and you'll reach the redeveloped Battersea Power Station, now full of shops, restaurants and riverside spaces, with its iconic chimneys towering overhead. Head north along Albert Embankment instead and you'll pass the Garden Museum and Lambeth Palace on the way towards the South Bank.
